title: Splicing deficiency is driven by genomic erosion in non-recombining algal mating-type chromosomes
experiments_summary:
1. Short-read RNA-seq analysis: Publicly available short-read RNA-seq data for four Mamiellales species (with chromosome-level genome assemblies and defined mating-type regions) were aligned to respective genomes using STAR v2.7.10b. Intron retention rates were quantified using rMATS v4.3.0 with '--allow-clipping --novelSS' parameters, comparing mating-type region genes to autosomal genes within each species.

2. Intron feature analysis: Introns were extracted from annotated CDS features in GTF files. Branchpoint windows (50 nt upstream) were retrieved and analyzed with DREME to identify enriched motifs. Splice-site flanking sequences, canonical splice-site frequencies, intron GC content, and intron lengths were compared between mating-type and autosomal regions using Fisher's exact tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.

3. Mixed-effects modeling of intron retention variance: A linear mixed-effects model with gene ID as a random effect was fit to intron retention ratios to partition variance attributable to gene-level versus intron-level effects and calculate intra-gene correlation.

4. Random Forest classification of intron retention: Binary classifiers (retained intron ratio ≥0.025 vs. <0.025) were trained separately on mating-type and autosomal introns for each species. Features included TPM, intron length, GC content, distance from TSS, canonical splice-site identity, frame disruption status, and one-hot encoded splice-site flanking sequences. Gene-level 80/20 train-test splitting was used, hyperparameters were optimized via randomized search with 3-fold cross-validation, and a minimal feature set was identified using elbow detection (Kneed algorithm). Partial dependence plots were generated for selected features. Models were evaluated by AUC-ROC and F1 score.

5. Chromatin and methylation analysis (M. pusilla): MNase-seq coverage and CpG methylation fraction data from a prior study (GEO accessions GSM1134620 and GSM1134621) were integrated to compare nucleosome occupancy and DNA methylation levels between mating-type and autosomal regions.

6. Long-read isoform sequencing (R2C2) of M. pusilla: Strain RCC834 was cultured under controlled conditions (18°C, 14h light:10h dark, L1 medium). RNA was extracted using Trizol/chloroform followed by RNeasy purification. Full-length cDNA libraries were prepared via SmartScribe reverse transcription with indexed oligo-dT primers and a template-switching oligo, then PCR-amplified. Libraries were circularized by Gibson assembly using a dsDNA splint, treated with exonucleases to remove uncircularized molecules, subjected to rolling circle amplification with Phi29 polymerase, debranched with T7 endonuclease, size-selected (>3 kb with ProNex beads), and sequenced on an ONT PromethION R10.4 flow cell. Raw reads were basecalled with Dorado, converted to consensus reads and demultiplexed with C3POa v3.2, and isoforms were identified and quantified with Mandalorion v4.6. Isoform calls were refined using SQANTI3 QC with '--isoAnnotLite'.

7. Alternative splicing event classification from R2C2 isoforms: For each M. pusilla gene with ≥2 isoforms, alternative 5' splice sites (A5SS), alternative 3' splice sites (A3SS), exon skipping (SE), and retained introns (RI) were identified by comparing junction coordinates across isoforms. Per-gene event counts were compared between mating-type and autosomal regions.

8. Isoform diversity and transcript termination analysis: Isoform usage evenness was quantified using the Shannon diversity index normalized by maximum possible diversity. Linear models incorporating log-transformed TPM, intron number, and mating-type region status as predictors were fit to isoform count and evenness. Polyadenylation site diversity was modeled with a Poisson GLM and transcription start site diversity with a GLM, both including mating-type region status as the main predictor.

9. Protein function assessment: CDS lengths of all isoforms were compared to canonical annotations. Functional domains and gene ontology terms were annotated for all M. pusilla proteins using InterProScan v5.59-91.0 with '-goterms'. The proportions of isoforms retaining specified percentages of annotated domains and GO terms were compared between mating-type and autosomal gene isoforms using Mann-Whitney U tests and GLMs.

10. Oligo-dT mispriming control: A logistic regression model (P(has_IR) ~ perc_A + gene_id) was fit to 1,393 isoforms from 164 mating-type genes containing both IR and non-IR isoforms, where perc_A was the percentage of adenine in the 20 bp genomic window downstream of each isoform's transcript termination site, to test whether downstream A-content predicted intron retention. Additionally, Mandalorion's A-content filter (Acutoff=0.5) was applied during isoform calling to discard reads with >50% adenine in the downstream 20 bp window.
